correctness.rationale: For K5^(3)-free G on exactly seven vertices, every five-set contains missing triple. With t missing triples and upper four-shadow s, c(G)=99-t-s exactly. Normalize a missing triple by vertex permutation. The C++17 certificate exhausts all C(34,t-1) possibilities for each 1<=t<=8; feasible t<=4 nonexistent; feasible t=5/6/7 have minimum s=17/19/20 respectively. All normalized 8-family shadows have size>=16, extending by monotonicity to t>=8. Thus t+s>=22 globally. Exactly five normalized score-22 cases have t=5,s=17, each verified to be a complete 3+4 internal missing-triple family; all 35 labelled balanced constructions attain equality. An independent Python census reproduces covering counts and the equality classification for t<=7. All boundaries and enumeration completeness are explicitly checked.

value.rationale: This determines the complete natural finite clique-count extremum and all 35 labelled equality objects at the first odd order beyond a known six-vertex result. It tests the genuine balanced-bipartite conjectural extremal structure at an order not covered by the quantified large-n theorem and improves what the general conjectural numerical bound alone could imply at n=7. Its exact finite cutoff and symmetry classification are mathematically motivated even without generalizing to all orders; it is neither a renamed graph nor an arbitrary restricted parameter slice.
